one_month_reasoning: Dycom's own Q3 FY27 report is expected around 2026-11-23 (Earnings Whispers, unconfirmed), i.e. after the 2026-11-08 window, so no company-specific earnings event falls inside it. Scheduled items in the window: (1) Loudoun County Board vote on 2026-10-20 to enact an up-to-12-month pause on data center/substation legislative approvals retroactive to 2026-09-15 (Loudoun release; Venable) - widely telegraphed since July and largely priced, mild negative headline risk for the DMV-concentrated Building Systems segment; (2) late-October telecom (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen = ~50% of revenue) and hyperscaler Q3 reports, whose capex/fiber commentary is read across to DY (prediction markets price Amazon 2026 capex > $190B at 95.5%, so a capex disappointment is not the base case); (3) peer contractor Q3 results (MTZ, PWR) in late Oct/early Nov. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: strong negative price momentum (new 52-week low $263.36 in the week of 2026-09-28) versus reversal after a ~52% drawdown and clustered small insider buys at $281-297. With no strong directional edge I centre the distribution at ~$270 (essentially spot) with log-sigma 0.15 (annual 52% / 3.5), a symmetric spread.

fair_value.method: Blend of horizon P/E (70%): est. NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $21.50 x 17x = $365.5, and P/FCF (30%): est. NTM FCF/share $18.60 x 18x = $334.8; blended ~$356. Multiples sit below the 11-peer median forward P/E of 21.2x (Finviz), close to the closest peer MasTec (17.2x), reflecting customer concentration, leverage and DMV data-center permitting risk.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon (Oct-2027) NTM adj EPS $21.50 x 17.0x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus table; cross-check: Finviz Fwd P/E 13.19 at $269.23 implies next-FY EPS of 269.23/13.19 = $20.41 (source 7).

Well below Finviz EPS next-5Y growth of 28.42% and FY28 consensus growth of ~22% (source 6): Power Solutions anniversaries in FY28, the $150M wireless deferral shifts revenue into FY28 (flattering FY28, not FY29), Communications margins are under investment pressure (call), while the ~$20B long-haul opportunity is 'back-half loaded towards the end of the decade' (call) and supports continued growth.
At 2027-10-09 the NTM window is ~1 quarter of FY28 + ~3 quarters of FY29: 20.78 x (1 + 0.75 x 0.12) = $22.65.
Communications adj EBITDA margin fell 134bp y/y to 13.6% and management declined to guide FY28 Communications growth; Q4 seasonality flagged as uncertain. 22.65 x 0.95 = $21.52, rounded to $21.50.

11-peer forward P/E median 21.19x, range 11.02-35.78x (Finviz). 17x is inside the range, ~20% below the median and in line with MasTec (17.19x), the closest telecom+power peer which is also levered. Discount reflects factors that persist through the horizon: ~50% revenue from three telecom customers (AT&T 25.4%, Verizon 14.0%, Lumen 10.8%; 10-K), pro forma net leverage ~2.3x vs mostly net-cash building-systems peers (call; debt $2,819.7M less cash $340.1M = ~$2.48B net, release), and Building Systems concentration in the DMV where data-center moratoria/pauses are spreading (Venable July and Sept 2026). Not 13-15x (today's level) because next-year EPS growth (19.68%) is at/above the peer median (19.36%, Finviz) and NTM backlog is up 41% y/y ($6,472M vs $4,604M).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM FCF/share $18.60 x 18x P/FCF (5.6% FCF yield)

inputs_detail.derivation: Finviz screener value for DY at 2026-10-09 close.
Uses Finviz consensus EPS next-year growth as a proxy for FCF growth: 15.54 x 1.1968 = $18.60.

Peer P/FCF (Finviz) median 28.76x, range 10.09-69.76x; 18x is inside the range near DY's own 17.33x, discounted for working-capital volatility of contractor FCF and the same concentration/leverage/DMV factors as the P/E method.

bear.story: DMV permitting pauses (Loudoun, Prince William, Prince George's, Montgomery, Maryland EO) spread and slow Power Solutions' follow-on awards; a second wireless deferral or AT&T/Lumen fiber pacing cut; Communications margins keep slipping. FY28 EPS lands ~$17-18 and the stock de-rates to ~11x, ~ $195.

base.story: Backlog ($12.2B, NTM $6.5B) converts; FY27 delivered near $17 consensus and FY28 guide (Mar-2027) frames ~$20 EPS incl. the $150M deferred wireless; DMV moratoria affect new approvals, not the in-backlog work. Multiple recovers only partly (~14-15x NTM EPS ~$21) because the moratorium overhang and leverage persist: ~ $300.

bull.story: Long-haul/hyperscaler awards enter backlog, BEAD construction starts in earnest in 2027, Building Systems keeps high-teens/low-20s margins and expands beyond the DMV; consensus EPS is beaten and the multiple re-rates toward the peer median (~19-20x NTM EPS ~$22.5): ~ $440.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 11.02x (LMB) to 35.78x (PWR) across 11 peers (Finviz, 2026-10-09); P/FCF 10.09x-69.76x (median 28.76x). Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available from a free source I could open and verify, so it is left null rather than substituted with trailing figures.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DY trades at 13.19x forward P/E (Finviz) vs peer median 21.19x, the second-lowest in the set. Our 17x target multiple is ~20% below the median, in line with MasTec (17.19x), and inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount (not premium), argued on factors that persist through Oct-2027: (1) ~50% of revenue from three telecom customers (AT&T 25.4%, Verizon 14.0%, Lumen 10.8%, FY26 10-K) whose program timing just moved $150M of wireless revenue into FY28; (2) pro forma net leverage ~2.3x after the Power Solutions/NTI deals vs net-cash balance sheets at EME, FIX, IESC, STRL, AGX, MYRG (MTZ, also levered, trades at a similar 17.2x); (3) Building Systems (24.5% margin, high-growth) is concentrated in the Greater Washington DC/MD/VA market where Loudoun, Prince William, Prince George's, Montgomery and Maryland's governor have moved to pause or tighten data-center approvals (Venable, Loudoun), with legislative changes likely in the 2027 sessions. Growth does not justify a discount: DY's EPS next-year growth (19.68%) is at or above the peer median. The discount is not widened to today's ~13x because the near-term backlog already covers most of FY28 Building Systems revenue ($1,110M NTM backlog) and the moratoria target new approvals.

thesis_break_reason: $205 is ~10x FY28 consensus EPS ($20.78) and ~24% below spot; below it the market would be pricing a structural earnings reset (e.g. FY28 EPS in the mid-teens), not just a multiple squeeze. Fundamental triggers that would put it there: FY28 guidance (Mar-2027) implying flat-to-down EPS, a second wireless/fiber program deferral or loss at AT&T/Verizon/Lumen, Building Systems backlog shrinking as DMV pauses bite into awards (rather than only future approvals), or covenant/leverage stress above ~3x.

key_uncertainties: How far DMV data-center pauses reach into Power Solutions' award pipeline vs only new zoning approvals; whether moratoria spread to other states (Polymarket prices 10-20% per state by end-2027).
Whether the $150M wireless deferral is a timing shift (management) or the start of reduced carrier spending.
Communications margin trajectory as DY invests in capacity ahead of long-haul and BEAD work.
Leverage (~2.3x) if the cycle turns: Polymarket US-recession-by-end-2027 at 32.5% (thin market) vs 6.5% by end-2026.
Momentum/positioning: the stock fell from $566 to $269 while peers (PWR, FIX) held high multiples, so sentiment rather than earnings drives much of the variance.
Research limits: Reddit (403) and X were not reachable; Dycom's job board loads dynamically and could not be counted; peer forward EV/EBITDA not available from an open source.
reasoning: Starting point: DY at $269 is 13.2x Finviz forward P/E and ~13x FY28 consensus EPS ($20.78) after falling 52% from the $566 late-May peak, while specialty-contractor peers trade at a 21x median and Comfort Systems/Quanta at 28.5-35.8x. Fundamentals reported through Q2 FY27 are strong (revenue +45.6%, adj EPS $5.29, backlog $12.2B, NTM backlog +41%, FY27 guide raised), so the de-rating is DY-specific. My lane work points to why: (a) the sharp late-July leg ($440 to $370 in the week of 2026-07-27, Twelve Data) followed Loudoun's 2026-07-22 vote to study a data-center pause and a wave of DMV moratoria (Prince George's 2-yr, Montgomery, Chesapeake; Venable July) - and Dycom's high-margin Building Systems segment (Power Solutions) is a Greater Washington DC/MD/VA data-center electrical contractor; September brought Loudoun's 12-month pause plan, Prince William's by-right elimination and both governors' executive orders (Venable Sept, Loudoun release); (b) the Q2 print added a $150M wireless deferral and a 134bp Communications margin decline (call), triggering a -21.6% week and target cuts (Fool). Offsets: demand in the region is still large (Dominion: >53 GW in contracting stages, ~12 GW under ESAs, +5 GW in H1 2026), DMV pauses target new approvals while DY's Building Systems NTM backlog is $1.11B, and three insiders (CEO, two directors) bought in the open market at $281-297 in September - small dollar amounts but the first cluster of buys, a mild positive. Prediction markets give modest macro and contagion risk (US recession by end-2026 6.5% on $2.3M volume; by end-2027 32.5% on a thin $10k market; state data-center moratoria by end-2027 ~10-20%). Valuation: P/E 17x on horizon NTM EPS $21.50 ($365) and P/FCF 18x on $18.60 ($335), blended fair value ~$356 (+32%). I do not put full weight on fair value because negative momentum, unresolved DMV policy and leverage can keep the discount for the whole year; scenarios: bear $195 (30%), base $300 (45%), bull $440 (25%), each with log-dispersion 0.25-0.30, giving a mean ~$304, median ~$295 and an effective volatility near 43% (below the 52% realized, which was inflated by the earnings gap and the AI-momentum unwind). Ladder tails kept non-trivial on both sides (P>=$538 ~6%, P>=$162 ~92%). Sell-side targets ($521 avg) were treated as evidence of estimate levels, not as the answer. Lane share: 11 of 22 sources (50%) are alternative-lane kinds (prediction markets, independent law-firm newsletters, local-government agenda, insider-flow Form 4s); the rest are filings for reported facts and single data pages for consensus and peer multiples - below the 60% target because Reddit/X blocked access and the job board could not be read, which I note as a research limitation.
